correctness.rationale: The pointwise slope rule gives exact admissible intervals at and only at critical knots. Critical-gap ratio constraints form a forest on integer gap indices, allowing every prescribed ratio jointly, including zero and one limits, via positive vanishing secant differences. Integration realizes genuine pointwise data perturbations. Hermite basis linearity gives an exact finite product set, and nonadjacent critical supports give 4/27 max and 16/27 sum formulas. Exact analytical maxima and the separate rational checker support these computations; local convergence and empty-set cases are explicit.

originality.rationale: A full inspected 2019 technical article proves the qualitative zero-weight Akima discontinuity, so that is explicitly treated as prior art. The 2026 indexed Akima result gives a single-signal range defect 2/27. Neither source gives independent simultaneous limiting derivatives at every critical knot, the entire product-box cluster family, nor the sharp cross-cluster uniform and total-variation diameters 4/27 and 16/27. The present proof uses a forest of constraints on zero secant gaps, not just the one-knot example. The original 1970 full article remains an access risk.
residual_risks: Full original Akima (1970) and its earlier 1969 report were not available for complete primary-text comparison; a historical equivalent cluster classification cannot be excluded.
Indexed and semantically searched findings may omit older specialized nomenclature (limiting divided-difference selector, cluster of cubic Hermite interpolants).
Sharp numerical diameters concern \(C^1_{\mathrm{loc}}\) cluster values at fixed base data, not a finite-perturbation Lipschitz norm or global convergence for unbounded perturbations.

value.rationale: Sensitivity of a standard piecewise-cubic interpolant at its branch-denominator degeneracy is a mathematically motivated stability problem. A previously known single-counterexample does not determine whether multiple corner defects are mutually compatible or how their variations combine. The theorem gives the full simultaneous limit set, a sharp L-infinity diameter, and an exact additive BV diameter for arbitrary finite critical-corner configurations. The forest compatibility mechanism is structural and applicable to assessing alternative slope selectors.
